segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: After he had finished all his sayings in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now a centurion had a slave who was highly valued by him, and this slave was sick and about to die.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he heard about Jesus, he sent elders of the Jews to him, asking him to come and save his slave.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they came to Jesus, they pleaded with him earnestly, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “He is worthy to have you grant him this,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Jesus went with them. He was already not far from the house when the centurion sent friends to say to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not fit to have you come under my roof.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: That is why I did not consider myself worthy even to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: For I too am a man placed under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes; and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes; and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When Jesus heard this, he was amazed at him. Turning to the crowd that was following him, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the slave in good health.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Soon afterward he went to a town called Nain, and his disciples and a large crowd went with him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: As he came near the gate of the town, a man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow. A sizable crowd from the town was with her.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Lord saw her, he was moved with compassion for her and said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do not weep.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he came up and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still. He said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Young man, I say to you, rise!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “A great prophet has risen among us!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “God has visited his people!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This report about him spread through the whole of Judea and all the surrounding region.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: John’s disciples reported all these things to him. Calling two of his disciples to him, John

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: sent them to the Lord to ask,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the men came to him, they said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “John the Baptist has sent us to you to ask, ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect another?’”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In that hour he healed many people of diseases, afflictions, and evil spirits, and to many who were blind he granted sight.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: the blind see again, the lame walk, those with skin disease are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, the poor have good news announced to them.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When John’s messengers had left, he began to speak to the crowds about John:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: What, then, did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who wear splendid clothing and live in luxury are in royal palaces.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: What, then, did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Look, I am sending my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way ahead of you.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: (And all the people who heard, even the tax collectors, vindicated God, having been baptized with John’s baptism.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law rejected God’s purpose for themselves, not having been baptized by him.)

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “To what, then, shall I compare the people of this generation, and what are they like?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: They are like children sitting in the marketplace and calling out to one another, saying, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, ‘He has a demon.’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The Son of Man has come eating and drinking, and you say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Yet wisdom is vindicated by all her children.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him, and he went into the Pharisee’s house and reclined at the table.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was a woman in the town who was a sinner. When she learned that he was reclining at the table in the Pharisee’s house, she brought an alabaster jar of perfume

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and stood behind him at his feet, weeping. With her tears she began to wet his feet, and she kept wiping them with the hair of her head, kissing his feet and anointing them with the perfume.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what kind of woman this is who is touching him—that she is a sinner.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus answered him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Simon, I have something to say to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, say it.”

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Since they had nothing to repay him with, he canceled the debts of both. Which of them, then, will love him more?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Simon answered,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I suppose the one for whom he canceled the larger debt.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And he said to him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “You have judged rightly.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then, turning to the woman, he said to Simon,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Do you see this woman? I came into your house; you gave me no water for my feet, but she has wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You gave me no kiss, but she, from the time I came in, has not stopped kissing my feet.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason, I tell you, her sins, many as they are, have been forgiven, for she loved much. But the one who is forgiven little loves little.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to her,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Your sins have been forgiven.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Those reclining at the table with him began to say among themselves,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Who is this, who even forgives sins?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he said to the woman,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

notes.note: Older versions have “servant.” The Greek word names a person owned by another, and a first-century reader would have understood “slave”; several modern versions agree. In verse 7 the centurion uses a different word, which can mean “boy,” “child,” or “servant,” and is rendered “servant” there.
This is the same Greek word that in the plural is usually rendered “Gentiles.” In the singular it means a people or nation, and here the Jewish elders use it of their own people.

The wording matches the Greek version of 1 Kings 17:23, where Elijah restores a widow’s dead son and gives him to his mother. Readers who knew that story would hear the echo, which helps explain the crowd’s response in the next verse: “A great prophet has risen among us!”

Most versions keep “lepers.” The Greek term names people with the range of scaly skin conditions regulated in Leviticus 13–14, which made a person ritually unclean; that is why they are “cleansed” and not simply healed. Modern “leprosy” (Hansen’s disease) is narrower and may not even be included. Scholars widely agree on this, though many translations keep the familiar word and explain it in a footnote.

notes.phrase: have good news announced to them
notes.traditional: have the gospel preached to them
notes.note: The Greek verb was an ordinary word for announcing good news, while “gospel” is now a religious term or a book title; many modern versions also have “good news” here. The whole list echoes Isaiah’s pictures of the time of God’s salvation (Isaiah 35:5–6; 61:1), which is the point of the answer sent to John.

The verb comes from a word for a trap or obstacle and means being tripped up in one’s trust or loyalty. “Offended” now suggests hurt feelings, which is too weak. Modern versions divide here between “takes no offense at me” and “does not stumble on account of me.”

The verb belongs to a single Greek word family that English splits in two (“righteous” and “just,” “righteousness” and “justice,” “justify”). Here it means to declare someone to be in the right: by accepting John’s baptism the people affirmed that God’s call through John was right. Many modern versions paraphrase as “acknowledged God’s justice” or “declared God just.” The same verb returns in verse 35.

Verses 29–30 are taken here, with the punctuation of the Greek edition translated, as the narrator’s aside. They can also be read as a continuation of Jesus’s own words about John. It is likewise unclear whether what the people “heard” was John’s preaching or what Jesus has just said.

The word names men learned in the Law of Moses and its interpretation, a group overlapping with the scribes. “Lawyer” now suggests an attorney representing clients in court. Several modern versions use “experts in the law”; others keep “lawyers.”

notes.phrase: stood behind him at his feet
notes.note: At a formal meal guests reclined on low couches, leaning on the left elbow with their feet stretched out away from the table. This is how the woman could stand behind Jesus and still reach his feet.
A denarius was a Roman silver coin, roughly a day’s wage for a laborer. The two debts are therefore well over a year’s wages and about two months’ wages.

The Greek conjunction can give either the cause of something or the evidence for it. The parable, in which love follows the canceling of a debt, and the second half of the verse favor the second sense: her great love shows that she has been forgiven. Most interpreters read it this way, though an older reading takes her love as the reason for her forgiveness.

Can mean child, boy or servant, and is used both of household servants and of Jesus and David as God’s “servant,” so renderings vary widely.
Recurs across the Synoptic Gospels of Jesus and in parables, and versions vary between “have compassion,” “feel pity” and “his heart went out.”
Appears in all the anointing accounts and in Revelation, and versions vary between “ointment,” “perfume” and “perfumed oil.”
Covers granting a favor, canceling a debt and forgiving; in Paul it stands near ἀφίημι, so a ruling is needed on when to use “forgive.”
